The '''''Rendiconti di Matematica e delle sue Applicazioni''''' (''Reports on Mathematics and its applications'') is an open access [[peer review|peer-reviewed]] [[mathematics journal]], jointly published by the "Guido Castelnuovo" Department of Mathematics of the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] and by the [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi]],<ref name="publishers">See {{harv|Zappa|1984|p=12}} and {{harv|Roghi|2005|p=10}}.</ref> established in 1913.<ref name="founded.in">{{harv|Bacciotti|1998|p=309}}, {{harv|The Editorial Board|2016a}}.</ref> The Journal started his publications a year after, in 1914, and his first director was [[Vito Volterra]].<ref name="1st.issue&dir">According to the [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|2016a}}|Journal "Historical Notes" (]]2016): see  also {{harv|Ceccherini|1970|loc=p. 3}}.</ref>

It publishes research articles in [[Pure mathematics|pure]] and [[applied mathematics]], without imposing restrictions on the length of the work: for this reason, the submission of surveys, articles of foundational nature and [[doctoral dissertation]]s is also encouraged.<ref>See the journal editorial policy statement at the [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|2016}}|journal home page (]]2016).</ref> As in every [[peer reviewed]] journal, every article is refereed, and the journal adheres to the [[European Mathematical Society Code of Practice|EMS Code of Practice]].<ref name="homeNotes">([[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|2016}}|Journal home page (]]2016).</ref>

The journal is [[abstracting and indexing|abstracted and indexed]] by ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'',  ''[[Zentralblatt MATH]]'' and ''[[Scopus]]''.

==Historical notes==

===Foundation and the first four series===

{{blockquote
|text='''ART. I'''.<br>
È fondato, presso la Facoltà di Scienze della R. Università di Roma, un Istituto avente lo scopo di diffondere la cultura matematica e di promuovere studi e ricerche matematiche. Esso prenderà il nome di «Seminario matematico».<ref>(English translation) Comma I. "An Institute is established at the Faculty of Sciences of the Royal University of Rome with the aim of spreading mathematical culture and promoting mathematical studies and research. It will be named the «Mathematical Seminar»".</ref>
|source= From the Rules of the seminar published in {{harv|Seminario Matematico della Facoltà di Scienze della R. Università di Roma|1914|loc=p. 3}}.
}}

The journal was founded in 1913 as the press organ of the "Seminario Matematico della Facoltà di Scienze della Reale Uninversità di Roma":<ref name="founded.in" /> its first director ([[Editor in chief]]) was Vito Volterra,<ref name="1st.issue&dir" /> who held this position from its foundation to the year 1921. The direction passed to [[Guido Castelnuovo]] who held it from 1921 to 1922:<ref>{{harvtxt|Ceccherini|1970|loc=pp. IX, 3}}.</ref> with the beginning of and during the publishing of the whole second and third series of the journal, from 1922 to 1935 [[Federigo Enriques]] was the director.<ref>{{harvtxt|Ceccherini|1970|loc=pp. IX, 9, 17}}.</ref> During fourth series of the journal, at the starting of which it underwent its first name change, the direction passed to [[Gaetano Scorza]], who held it until his death in 1939.<ref>{{harv|Ceccherini|1970|loc=pp. IX, 19}}</ref>

===The INdAM and its influence===
The founding of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica]] in 1939, under the decisive influence of [[Francesco Severi]],<ref>According to {{harvtxt|De Concini|2005|p=VII}} and {{harvtxt|Zappa|1984|p=12}}, who also who precisely states that:-"''Proprio in quell'anno 1939–1940, Severi aveva costituito l'Istituto di Alta Matematica''" ({{langx|en|Just in that year 1939–1940, Severi constituted the Istituto di Alta Matematica}}).</ref> had important consequences on the "Rendiconti del Seminario Matematico". On 23 November 1939, during its first meeting, the Scientific [[Council]]<ref>"{{langx|it|Il Consiglio Scientifico}}" {{harv|Roghi|2005|p=8}}.</ref> of the then newborn institute,<ref>The members of the council were Francesco Severi (the [[President (education)|president]]), [[Luigi Fantappiè]], [[Giulio Krall]] as members of the institute, Enrico Bompiani and [[Mauro Picone]] as member chosen by the [[Faculty of Sciences]] of the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] {{harv|Roghi|2005|p=8}}.</ref> considering the need of a means to publish the results of the research done by the members and the students working at the institute,<ref name="Roghi.p10">{{harv|Roghi|2005|p=10}}.</ref> decided to merge the needed means and the already existing journal in one single entity, giving birth to the "Rendiconti di Matematica e delle sue Applicazioni".<ref name="Roghi.p10" /> Entrusted with this double function the fifth series of the journal, from the first volume published in 1940<ref>{{harv|Ceccherini|1970|p=26}}.</ref> to the first [[Issue (periodical)|issue]] of the fourth volume published in 1943,<ref>{{harv|Ceccherini|1970|p=42}}.</ref> included a section listing the programs of the INdAM courses of the current [[academic year]]<ref>"''Programmi dei corsi...''" ({{langx|en|Course programs...}}): see {{harv|Ceccherini|1970|pp=28–29, 31–32, 37–39, 45–46}}.</ref> as well as section listing the research problems proposed by the lecturers currently working at the institute.<ref>"''Problemi, risultati e discussioni (lavori di seminario)''" ({{langx|en|Problems, results and discussions (Seminar wors)}}): see {{harv|Ceccherini|1970|pp=27–28, 29–31, 32–34, 35–37, 39–41, 43–45}} and  also the description of the activities at the INdAM in the early 1940s given by {{harvtxt|Zappa|1984|p=12}}.</ref>

This is a [[monograph]]ic [[Serial (literature)|fascicle]] published on the "Bollettino della Unione Matematica Italiana", describing the history of the "Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi" from its foundation in 1939 to 2003: it was written by [[Gino Roghi]] and includes a presentation by Salvatore Coen and a preface by Corrado De Concini. It is almost exclusively based on [[source text|sources]] from the institute archives: the wealth and variety of materials included, jointly with its [[Addendum#In books|appendices]] and [[Index (publishing)|indexes]], make this monograph a useful reference not only for the history of the [[institute]] itself, but also for the history of many [[mathematician]]s who taught or followed the institute courses or simply worked there.
